obligations.note: routes.py adds Route("POST", "/payees/{id}/reopen", "manage_payees", mfa=False), and manage_payees is in the approved privileged action list. The exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on exactly this route, and no valid exception covers it.

The new state-changing LedgerService.reopen_payee calls self._audit(actor, "reopen_payee", f"payee:{payee_id}"), which records user_id, action, target and clock time. This is the same pattern as close_payee.
Store.reopen_payee only updates status and closed_at. It writes no NPI column, so sealing of NPI fields is unaffected.
The new statement "UPDATE payees SET status = 'open', closed_at = NULL WHERE id = ?" is a fixed string with payee_id bound as a parameter. No statement text is built from data.
Ticket CHG-25323 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-22, before review. Its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover app.py, routes.py, service.py and store.py.
The code_review approval is from Mara Costa, a payments change_approver. She is a different person from the author, Sofia Santos.
Both approvals name the head commit fd18083, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json for the head commit reports result "failure". The JUnit report shows the registered MFA-1 control test failing. The report is also timestamped 2026-10-23 on a personal machine, which predates the head commit.
The change touches security-sensitive components (payments.routes, payments.http, payments.store). Kofi Mensah, a security_reviewer, gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
No protected paths (controls/, tests/controls/, ci/) are changed, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and change.json has emergency=false, so no post-implementation review is due.
EXC-0237 was requested and 'approved' by the same person, Sofia Santos. She is the author and does not hold the risk_owner role, so the exception is invalid and cannot excuse the MFA-1 deviation.
Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1, covering routes.py) lapses because routes.py changed in behaviour. The replacement evidence, the same exhaustive control test, fails on the head commit.

summary: The change adds a privileged route, POST /payees/{id}/reopen (action manage_payees), with MFA disabled, which violates MFA-1. The cited exception EXC-0237 is invalid because the requester self-approved it without the risk_owner role. The change's CI run on the head commit failed, including the registered exhaustive MFA control test, so testing (CHG-4) and evidence renewal (LAP-1) are not met. The ticket, independent code review and security review are otherwise in order, but the violations require rejection.
